findings.message: This fixes the instance, not the class. `AUDIT_HASH_KEY` covers the whole deployment, but `deploymentKey` only checks the target tenant's rows, and it skips the check when that tenant has no keyed v2 row yet. Your own documented setup always reaches that case: `tenant-add` and `user-add` write no audit rows, so the first `principal-add` on a new tenant meets an empty chain and writes under whatever key the operator typed. AC-1 in the test runs this exact path with no check. Fix: compare against the latest keyed v2 row anywhere in the deployment. The CLI runs as the schema owner, so it can read `core.audit_event` across tenants, or across `core.trace_event`. Refuse when the deployment has keyed rows and none of them reproduces. Only skip when the whole deployment has no keyed rows. Add a variant to the AC-3 table: a fresh tenant in a deployment that already has rows, plus the wrong key. The command must exit non-zero and write nothing.
findings.scenario: An existing deployment uses key K. The operator runs `tenant-add Acme`, then `user-add --tenant <acme> ...`, then `principal-add --tenant <acme> ...` with `AUDIT_HASH_KEY="w".repeat(32)`. Acme has no v2 rows, so the check is skipped and the command exits 0. It appends `auth.principal.create` with `actor_key` set to HMAC(w-key). Later `verifyAuditChain(acme, K)` reports value mismatch at seq 1. That row can't be verified or erased, because the table is append-only.
